What the band means, for the person it is about

Source: R/calculator.R
mm_band_text_self.Rd

A different piece of writing, not the same one with simpler words. Someone reading their own number is not weighing a decision about a third party; they are being told something about themselves by a machine, and the three things they need are what the number counts, what it cannot see, and what to do next.

Usage

mm_band_text_self(
  prob,
  threshold,
  level,
  subject,
  event = "the outcome",
  n_predictors = NULL
)

Arguments

prob, threshold

Probabilities.

level

The band.

subject

What one row is, in the singular.

event

What the outcome is, in the past tense, as it would complete "of 100 ..., 15 ___".

n_predictors

How many predictors the model holds, or NULL.

Value

A single string.

Details

So: no odds ratio, because a ratio of odds is not a fact anyone can hold about themselves. A count out of a hundred instead, for both the prediction and the reference, because "15 in 100" is the form of this quantity people read most reliably. The number of predictors is named, because the strongest honest thing to say about a low prediction is how little of an application the model actually saw. The low bands neither reassure nor commiserate: the number is reported, what the model could not see is named, and the reader is sent to someone who can advise them.
